meta.title: Context compression tiers
meta.description: Adds a Context compression page under Settings with five automatic compaction tiers (gentle, light, standard, aggressive, max). Picking a tier pushes its thresholdRatio and retainRatio into every mounted agent preset compaction engine immediately, so no restart is needed, and stores the choice in <DSH home>/compression-tiers/settings.json. The plugin also adds four agent tools: compression_tiers reads or changes the tier and accepts optional per-route headroom overrides; compression_context reports live occupancy, the tier threshold and the room left; compression_compact queues a proactive compaction that runs after the turn and resumes the conversation by itself; github_push publishes the current work — the session working directory by default — after a network probe and a secret scan, with a 60-second push deadline and a failure family plus whatever is still local when it fails. A [context] line at the conversation tail reports the same occupancy. Every tier keeps automatic pressure compaction on, and /compact remains available to the human. The lower half of the page also edits the global rules: it reads and atomically writes the official instruction file <DSH home>/AGENTS.md (the official dsh-agent-instructions plugin injects it into later sessions), and the system prompt carries the newest 2,000-character clip; agents get no tool to rewrite that file, only a save on the page writes it. The page also manages GitHub CLI: it detects a gh on PATH, downloads a managed pinned gh 2.76.2 copy (resumable, atomic install, rollback on failure), and runs the gh auth login --web device flow for the official change-request panel; the credential stays in gh's own store and the plugin never reads it. Limitations: the tiers are designed for windows of at least 256k tokens (the official 65,536-token headroom caps smaller windows); the plugin updates preset-isolated engines and leaves the host-plane row alone; remove any other plugin that manages the same compaction engines or the two will fight over the policy; the 1.4.x sidebar repository panel is gone, and several repositories are published from each session through github_push; changing a tier updates the engines live, but a browser reload may be needed to see the page again.
